Let the inputs $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit integers
where $n$ is the bit length of each input
Fix a digit width $b$, the number of bits in each radix digit
let $q=\lceil n/b\rceil$ be the number of radix digits of each input
Here $x_j$ is the $j$th radix digit of $x$
and $y_j$ is the $j$th radix digit of $y$

anchor.note: Indexed-sequence notation (an entry x_i of a list, as with x_j defined on this page), covered by the reader's discrete mathematics and algorithm analysis. Its meaning as the i-th radix digit follows only by renaming the index in the x_j definition; the page does not state it for x_i.
